implementation_notes: Scala derives the serializer at compile time: circe's Encoder/Decoder (or upickle's ReadWriter) turn the case-class graph into JSON, and a Slick MappedColumnType.base[Graph, String] - or a Doobie/skunk codec - registers the column mapping, so the pattern's mapper is carried by implicits rather than by a class. Recursive types need a lazy codec definition, and the derivation style (semiauto vs auto) has to stay consistent across the codebase or the payload shape silently diverges.
code_sketch:
implicit val graphCodec: Codec[Graph] = deriveCodec[Graph]
implicit val graphColumn: BaseColumnType[Graph] =
  MappedColumnType.base[Graph, String](
    g => g.asJson.noSpaces,
    s => decode[Graph](s).fold(throw _, identity))

diagrams.map(_.graph)        // TEXT column holding JSON
pitfalls: Recursive case classes need lazy codec definitions; a naive deriveCodec on a self-referential type fails to compile or diverges at runtime.
Printer and derivation options (dropNullValues, discriminator, semiauto vs auto) are part of the stored contract: changing them makes old payloads unreadable unless the reader tolerates both shapes.
An implicit codec that is visible for the entity but not for the query fails to compile at best and falls back to a different representation at worst.
